objective: Close the M120 independent-hammer accepted-but-dropped same-address RMW counterexample while retaining one accepted 96-lane signed19 vector update per cycle without depending on foundry SRAM read-during-write behavior.

motivation.counterexample: two consecutive same-address events were both accepted at the mapper service cut but the old accumulator accepted only one mapped update/write and raised a sticky fault
motivation.repair: when the next accepted update has the same block and row as the pending update, suppress the macro read and forward the just-computed signed19 write vector as the next base

architecture.same_address_behavior: accepted at II=1; no macro read on the undefined read-during-write edge; prior computed vector is forwarded into the next add
architecture.different_address_behavior: unchanged synchronous read plus one-cycle RMW pipeline
architecture.overflow_behavior: fail closed and suppress the overflowing write

paper_safe_statement: Commercial VCS verifies a same-address-forwarding signed19 accumulator in which all 1072 positive directed updates produce 1072 lane-memory writes and exact full-window commits, including a 16-update same-address II=1 chain whose 15 undefined macro reads are suppressed and replaced by forwarded bases. Reset recovery, retry deduplication, foundry macros and speedup remain outside this admission.
prohibited_claims: Do not claim persistence or exact-once delivery across reset.
Do not call the behavioral lane memory a foundry macro.
Do not infer cycle, physical or system speedup from this functional forwarding result.
Do not claim retry deduplication; distinct accepted interface transactions remain distinct updates.
